- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods; reduce forecast peaks when sentiment is high or trending up.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment periods; raise forecast lows when sentiment is negative or trending down.
- Model tends to overshoot after sharp price spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to prevent overreaction.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above or below recent 5–10 day average, adjust toward historical mean.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; dampen forecast volatility when sentiment is volatile or noisy.
- When sentiment is strongly positive but price is falling, reduce forecast slope; when sentiment is negative but price is rising, increase downward bias.
- Avoid forecasting extreme values (e.g., >75% above or below recent range) unless sentiment strongly supports it.
